nodes.label: Anonymous role held by everyone
nodes.rationale: Public means the role anonymous in read roles; everyone, signed in or not, holds it. Fixed: a user with only a custom role did not count as anonymous. Only superadmin can make a dashboard public.

nodes.label: Dashboards as data, not code
nodes.rationale: A dashboard is JSON (title, columns, refresh, read roles, edit roles, owner, widgets). Nothing an author saves is parsed as HTML or executed, so a saved dashboard can never run code.

nodes.label: Designer as form with move/size buttons and live preview

nodes.label: No UI upload of widget code
nodes.norm_label: no ui upload of widget code
nodes.rationale: Deliberate: with a strict content policy uploaded code could not run, and loosening the policy would give every designer the power of the studied product's pages.

nodes.label: Strict content policy (no inline script or style)
nodes.norm_label: strict content policy (no inline script or style)
nodes.rationale: Widgets rendered by server-shipped code keep the strict content policy on; loosening it for uploaded code would give every designer the power of the studied product's pages.

nodes.label: Studied product: pages are HTML/script code (ma-* components)
nodes.norm_label: studied product: pages are html/script code (ma-* components)
nodes.rationale: Pages that are code are powerful and dangerous. Anyone who can save a page can run script as every viewer, so edit permission is effectively administrator permission (stored-XSS class by design).

nodes.rationale: Adding a widget type is two small reviewable pieces: a validator registered with @widget(name) in durian/dashboards.py and a registerWidget(name, {...}) renderer in web/dashboards.js. Whoever runs the server installs them.

nodes.rationale: A dead link must not be hammered; wait grows by scale factor to a cap. A device that rejects one read only loses those points.
